name: Ariel
title: Envoy who secured Levites for the return journey from exile
summary: Ariel was one of the leaders whom Ezra sent to Iddo in Casiphia to obtain Levites and temple servants for the return journey to Jerusalem. When Ezra gathered the people at the river that flows to Ahava and discovered that there were no Levites among them, he sent Ariel and other prominent men with a message to recruit servants for God's house. The mission succeeded, and Levites and temple servants joined the group. The name Ariel means 'God's lion' or 'God's hearth' in Hebrew and is also used as a poetic name for Jerusalem by the prophet Isaiah.

keyEvents.title: Shortage of Levites discovered at the Ahava River
keyEvents.description: When Ezra assembled the people by the river flowing to Ahava, he realized there were no Levites among them. He decided to send leaders to recruit Levites for temple service.

keyEvents.title: Ariel is sent to Casiphia
keyEvents.description: Ezra sent Ariel and other prominent leaders to Iddo, the leader at the place called Casiphia, with instructions to bring servants for the house of God in Jerusalem. The mission succeeded, and Levites and temple servants joined the traveling group.

keyEvents.title: Fasting and prayer at the Ahava River
keyEvents.description: Before departing from Babylon, Ezra proclaimed a fast at the Ahava River to seek God's guidance and protection for the journey. The leaders of the traveling group, among whom Ariel was likely included, participated in this preparation.

versions.summary: Ariel was one of the leaders whom Ezra sent messengers to at the river flowing to Ahava, to obtain Levites and temple servants for the return journey to Jerusalem. He played an important role in ensuring there were enough servants for God's house before the great return from Babylon. The name Ariel means 'Lion of God' or 'God's hearth' and is also used as a poetic name for Jerusalem in Isaiah.
versions.title: Leader among those who returned from exile
versions.reason: [major] The description is imprecisely worded. Ezra did not send a message 'to' Ariel to obtain Levites – Ariel was one of those whom Ezra sent out to Casiphia. Thus, it was Ariel who was sent on the mission, not that he was summoned. Ezra 8:16 mentions Ariel as one of those Ezra sent.; [minor] The event concerning fasting and prayer at the Ahava River is contextually relevant, but Ariel is not explicitly mentioned in verses 21–23. It should be stated more clearly that Ariel's participation is implied rather than directly noted.; [minor] This event concerns the name 'Ariel' as a poetic designation for Jerusalem in Isaiah 29, not the person named Ariel in Ezra. It is an interesting connection, but it is a namesake link, not an event tied to this individual. Consider moving this to a footnote instead of presenting it as a key event.; [minor] Ariel can also be described as a 'messenger' or 'envoy,' since his role was specifically to be sent by Ezra to Casiphia. 'Leader' alone is somewhat vague.; [minor] The sentence 'Ariel was one of the leaders whom Ezra sent for' is misleading. Ezra did not send for Ariel – he was already present and was dispatched as a messenger. Ezra 8:16 states that Ezra sent Ariel (and others) to Iddo at Casiphia.

It is a reasonable assumption since he was one of the leaders, but it should be phrased more cautiously to avoid adding something the Bible does not directly say.

footnotes.text: The name Ariel (אֲרִיאֵל) is composed of 'ari' (lion) and 'El' (God), meaning 'Lion of God'. The name can also be interpreted as 'God's hearth' or 'God's altar', based on an alternative Hebrew root. In Isaiah 29:1, the name is used as a poetic designation for Jerusalem, likely referring to the temple's burnt offering altar.

Kasiphia, the place where Ariel was sent, has not been identified with certainty. The name may mean 'place of silver' (from Hebrew 'kesef' = silver). It was probably a Jewish settlement area in Babylonia where there was some form of religious center or school, since Levites and temple servants (Nethinim) were located there.

The Nethinim (temple servants) recruited through Ariel's mission were a group traditionally traced to non-Israelite peoples who were given to the temple service. According to rabbinic tradition, some of them were originally given by David and his leaders to serve the Levites (Ezra 8:20).

The river at Ahava, where Ezra gathered the people, has not been definitely identified but was likely a canal or tributary in the Babylonian canal system. It was a common meeting point for Jewish groups preparing for the return journey to Judah.
